text:
Aisha: Quick heads-up: Acme pilot RACI changed — they just asked for customer-managed KMS (BYO-KMS) + p95 < 120ms for generation at 1k rps. Need to confirm feasibility & pricing impact before EOW. Can SE/Eng weigh in? @Liam @Kai

Liam: Noted. From previous pilots BYO-KMS adds ~15–40ms depending on region and KMS latency. Also certs/TLS egress might require network changes. Do we have a recommended architecture or a proxy pattern? Suggest token caching at proxy layer.

Kai: Short answer: with our current 7B quant config, hitting 120ms p95 @1k rps is tight without batching/kv cache and lower precision. Options: more aggressive quant (int4), route hot traffic to reserved high-priority pool, or accept a higher p95. BYO-KMS latency depends on their KMS — we can mitigate with DEK caching.

Nora: Can we get a crisp acceptance criteria list we can share externally? Also will this change the pilot pricing? Sales needs a clear up-sell path if they require reserved capacity.

Aisha: Draft acceptance criteria to share:
- Functional: end-to-end generation for provided 200-query prompt set returns coherent outputs
- Performance: p95 latency <= 120ms for single-turn generation <=512 tokens at 1k RPS (burst to 2k)
- Security: BYO-KMS configured and DEK rotation verified
- Observability: traces + token-level cost breakdown enabled
Is that reasonable or too aggressive?

Liam: Add: error budget <= 1% 5xx over 24h. Also need to know if streaming responses are required — streaming changes latency profile.

Kai: If customer accepts fallback (e.g., degrade to 300ms or use smaller batch sizes under load) we can avoid reserved GPUs initially. If they want strict 100–120ms p95 with BYO-KMS, we'll probably need reserved nodes. Ballpark cost delta: +40–70% monthly for reserved capacity vs shared. I'll run numbers.

Aisha: Customer counter: they insist on "no more than 100ms p95" and insist on BYO-KMS. They're price sensitive. Can we propose a staged plan?

Liam: Staged plan suggestion:
- Phase 1: Functional POC with BYO-KMS, relaxed SLA (250ms p95), collect telemetry and confirm security integration
- Phase 2: Optimize (kv-cache, batching, quantization) target 120ms p95
- Phase 3: If 100ms p95 still required, move to reserved capacity and reprovision nodes
Sales addendum: pricing tiers by phase.

Kai: Perf sketch:
```
- Model: 7B quantized int8
- Baseline (shared pool): ~180ms p95 @1k rps
- With kv-cache + tuned batching: ~120–140ms p95
- With int4 + reserved GPU: ~90–110ms p95
```

Aisha: Next steps: Kai to send perf deltas + cost delta by EOD; Liam to outline network & KMS checklist; Nora to produce acceptance criteria doc for customer. I'll coordinate timeline with Acme and ask whether 100ms is absolute.

infra-bot: Reminder: open network ticket #INC-4321 created for VPC egress rule add. Assigned: eng-infra.

Liam: :thumbsup: I'll start the checklist. Quick Q: do we need an updated security questionnaire for BYO-KMS specifics (HSM, key rotation, residency)?

Nora: Yes — include key residency, rotation policy, DEK wrapping, audit log access, and HSM details. I'll append a BYO-KMS section to the security doc.

Aisha: Thanks team — I'll propose the staged plan to the customer and flag cost implications. If they hold firm on 100ms, we may need to fast-track reserved quote.
